scene: Dawn below Mount Purgatory — the four stars, Cato, washing the face and binding a rush
story: Dante and Virgil emerge from the underground passage onto the shore of the island of Mount Purgatory. The sky opens above them at the first light of dawn.
Dante sees four bright stars in the southern sky and feels the change from Hell's enclosed darkness to open air.
Cato of Utica, guardian of the mountain, confronts the travelers and asks how they have escaped the eternal prison.

Virgil explains that Dante is living and has been guided here at the request of a woman from Heaven. Cato permits them to continue and orders Virgil to wash Hell's grime from Dante's face and gird him with a humble rush.
Virgil leads Dante to the shore, washes his face with dew, and picks a flexible rush to bind him. In the poem the rush springs back where it was plucked.
With the first ascent preparation completed, Dante and Virgil turn toward the mountain; the arriving angelic boat and new souls belong to Purgatorio II.
